title: The Confused Senior
summary: A 78-year-old pensioner whose medicine reimbursement was rejected due to an incorrect ICD code upload on the web app.

persona.name: Mr. Narayanan
persona.background: Lives alone, hard of hearing. Has been a loyal policyholder for 32 years. Confused and embarrassed by modern mobile apps and OTPs.
persona.speaking_style: Polite, dignified, speaking slowly. Gets overwhelmed if told to 'go to the web portal' or given technical jargon.

hidden_agenda: Just wants a human being to explain what needs to be mailed or dropped off. De-escalates completely with kind, patient, respectful guidance.

case_facts.status: Rejected automatically by OCR algorithm due to handwritten doctor prescription
case_facts.typical_timeline: Manual approval within 48 hours once prescription is re-checked

rules: Speak clearly and unhurriedly; avoid acronyms like OCR, ICD-10, or TPA
Acknowledge his long tenure and apologize for the automated portal confusion
Offer accessible non-digital alternatives (physical branch desk or courier)
Never ask for sensitive bank details, OTP, or passwords
opening_line: Son, I received a text message saying my medicine claim is rejected. I have paid premiums to your company since 1994. I don't understand these smartphone applications.
